stories.title: IShowSpeed wins a third straight Streamer of the Year award
paragraphs: The November 12 Streamer Awards named IShowSpeed Streamer of the Year for the third year in a row. He also won Best IRL Streamer and Best Streamed Series.

Jynxzi took Gamer of the Year, Kai Cenat won League of Their Own, and Quackity received the Legacy Award. The sixth ceremony, hosted by QTCinderella and Caroline Kwan, covered creator collaborations, live events, and game-specific streaming.
The results are widely reported, although the corroborating report said the organizers' full results page was not accessible when it checked, and some special-category lists differ.

scoreNotes.general: The awards are a prominent creator-industry event, and the winners are new since Owl's prior preview.
scoreNotes.heat: A major annual streaming ceremony recognizes creators across genres, events, collaborations, and games; public attention is evident in post-event coverage and discussion.
scoreNotes.time: The ceremony and its results arrived within the current 24-hour window.
scoreNotes.ethos: Accessible post-event reports agree on the leading winners, but Nacionale said it could not access a complete official results list and relied on secondary tallies.

stories.title: TwitchCon San Diego opens with a packed weekend of creator shows
paragraphs: TwitchCon San Diego runs November 13–15. Its official schedule highlights a Saturday event where e.l.f.
Cosmetics and creator YonnaJay plan to gather hundreds of creators and fans for a Guinness attempt at the largest simultaneous Get Ready With Me.
The weekend also includes the QSMP Awards hosted by Quackity, Ironmouse's karaoke Open Stage, a Rocket League streamer-squad showdown, and Noxcrew's MC Championship.
The convention gives creators a concentrated live stage for competitions, community events, and brand activations. The schedule confirms what is planned, not the outcomes or attendance figures.

scoreNotes.general: The convention combines a large creator gathering with unusual live formats and several high-profile community events.
scoreNotes.heat: The official schedule features a Guinness record attempt with hundreds of creators and fans, alongside QSMP, Minecraft, Rocket League, and other creator programming.
scoreNotes.time: TwitchCon runs November 13–15, with the record attempt and several shows on Saturday and Sunday.
scoreNotes.ethos: Dates, event descriptions, and the record attempt come from TwitchCon's current official schedule; the attempt's result is not yet known.

stories.title: Brands struggle to coordinate their creator relationships
paragraphs: Axios reports that communications and marketing teams at brands can approach the same creator with separate campaigns, budgets, and expectations, undermining a relationship one team may have spent months building.
Creator-economy specialists and corporate communications executives told Axios that companies need a clear internal point of contact and agreement on goals before outreach.
The issue shows how creator partnerships are moving beyond one-off sponsored posts, while companies still lack consistent ways to coordinate work and judge its longer-term value.

scoreNotes.general: The report identifies a practical business challenge as companies bring creators into communications, marketing, and broader strategy.
scoreNotes.heat: Creator partnerships are a growing business area, but this article documents a management problem through interviews and one example rather than market-wide measurements.
scoreNotes.time: Axios published the interviews and case example inside the current 24-hour window.
scoreNotes.ethos: The article quotes named creator-economy and corporate communications leaders; it does not quantify how common the coordination problem is.

stories.title: Adobe and Disney expand their AI partnership across creative production
paragraphs: Adobe and Disney announced a multi-year alliance that gives Disney early access to Firefly, Firefly Foundry, Premiere, Photoshop, and Adobe engineering support.

The companies will develop custom generative models based on Disney characters, environments, and visual styles for production workflows. Disney says its Imagineering team already uses a Firefly Foundry model to turn hand-drawn concepts into rendered park-design art.

The partnership extends into Disney's StudioLAB and ESPN Edge. The companies describe faster concept work and new storytelling uses, but have not reported deployment results or the deal's financial terms.

scoreNotes.general: Two major media and software companies are extending a longstanding relationship into custom AI tools for studio, sports, and visitor experiences.
scoreNotes.heat: The deal reaches Disney's parks, cruise operations, ESPN, and StudioLAB, but neither company disclosed its value or measured results.
scoreNotes.time: The multi-year alliance was announced November 9, within the seven-day fallback window.
scoreNotes.ethos: Adobe's announcement documents the agreement and tools; the promised productivity and creative effects remain prospective.

stories.title: Black Forest Games buys its independence from Embracer
paragraphs: Black Forest Games has spun out of THQ Nordic, within Embracer Group, through a management buyout and is a founding member of the new studio group Third Signal.
The German developer has worked on Destroy All Humans! remakes and Giana Sisters: Twisted Dreams.
Its management team becomes a co-owner, and the studio says it will continue making and publishing games under its own label.

THQ Nordic and Black Forest Games will continue collaborating on development tasks. The announcement describes greater independence but does not name a new project or explain how the change affects staffing.

scoreNotes.general: A known German developer has left a major publishing group through a management buyout and helped form a new independent studio group.
scoreNotes.heat: The move affects a developer with established PC and console franchises and reflects continuing restructuring among game studios; future project plans remain undisclosed.
scoreNotes.time: Third Signal announced the buyout on November 11, within the preceding seven days.
scoreNotes.ethos: The studio's announcement and independent reporting confirm the transaction; neither provides a new slate or employment forecast.

stories.title: Big Walk's small AI-assisted fix becomes a major indie-game dispute
paragraphs: House House said it used an LLM sparingly near the end of Big Walk's development to help solve a difficult Unity bug. It estimates the use touched well under 0.1% of the game's code and says developers substantially modified the suggested fix.

The disclosure became public after the studio submitted the game to the Independent Games Festival, whose jury rules do not make the same distinction between AI-generated content and AI-assisted coding that Steam's disclosure form does.

Ars Technica reported support from some IGF judges and disappointment from other judges and players, as well as more than 400 negative Steam reviews. That documents a heated debate, not a universal player view or a confirmed change to Big Walk's sales.

scoreNotes.general: The disclosure has become a visible test of how players and game-industry juries define acceptable generative AI use.
scoreNotes.heat: Coverage documents an IGF jury split, vocal player criticism, and more than 400 negative Steam reviews, while the game's overall reception remained Very Positive.
scoreNotes.time: The disclosure and main backlash began earlier in the seven-day window and remained under discussion in reporting and public forums.
scoreNotes.ethos: House House's account and the amount of code are attributed to the developer; reported review activity and reactions do not represent every player.

citations.title: Big Walk developer reveals it used generative AI 'sparingly', estimates 'well under 0.1%' was actually coded using LLMs

stories.title: Golden Joystick winners split the spotlight across blockbusters and indies
paragraphs: Resident Evil Requiem won Ultimate Game of the Year at the 2026 Golden Joystick Awards, while Capcom was named Studio of the Year.

The 25-category results were spread across the field: indie games Meccha Chameleon and Valheim won multiple honors, while Resident Evil Requiem, Crimson Desert, and The Witcher 4 also took major categories.
The spread makes the awards a snapshot of audience and industry recognition across different game scales. The ceremony's honors do not establish comparative sales or player activity.

scoreNotes.general: The annual voting awards produced a broad set of winners, with both leading franchises and smaller games recognized.
scoreNotes.heat: The event distributes recognition across major releases, studios, independent games, and long-running titles, but no exceptional audience or voting total is reported here.
scoreNotes.time: The 2026 results were reported within the preceding seven days.
scoreNotes.ethos: GamesRadar's winners list supplies the category results; awards reflect the ceremony's voting and judging process, not sales or player counts.
